title: Unit-normalized inverse-image comparison on localized sheaf sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be small categories in universe $u$, equipped with Grothendieck topologies $J$ and $K$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $U:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous (precomposition carries sheaves to sheaves) and representably flat (for every $d$, the category of arrows $d\to U(c)$ is cofiltered). Take set sheaves in universe $u+1$, and let $L$ be literally left Kan extension along $U^{\mathrm{op}}$ followed by $K$-sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. For $V\in\mathcal C$, let $Q_V$ and $Q_{U(V)}$ denote restriction to the localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. There exist a functor $H:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/V)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D/U(V))$, a natural family of presheaf maps $\eta_F:F\to (\operatorname{Over.post}U)^{\mathrm{op}}\circ H(F)$, and a natural isomorphism $e:H\circ Q_V\cong Q_{U(V)}\circ L$, such that for every global sheaf $F$, every $q:W\to V$, and $x\in F(W)$, the component of $e_F$ at $U(q)$ takes $\eta_{Q_VF,q}(x)$ to the actual unit $(F\to U^{\mathrm{op}*}L(F))_W(x)$ of the Kan-extension/sheafification adjunction. Naturality of $\eta$ means $\eta_G\circ f=H(f)\circ\eta_F$, with the precomposition on the right understood explicitly. No tower, coefficient rings, bases, or limit comparison is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: Form the disjoint-union presheaf S(A)(W)=Σ(q:W→V),A(q) and its projection to the lifted representable hV. Let P be left Kan extension along U.op followed by K-sheafification. On the target slice take the fibre of P(S(A))→P(hV) at the restriction of the actual-unit image of idV. Naturality preserves fibres; separatedness of the base sheaf proves that the resulting subfunctor is a sheaf. This constructs H and its action on arrows explicitly.

proof.text: Apply the actual unit to the pair (q,x). Naturality for the projection gives the fibre condition; naturality for the sigma map gives naturality of the family η. Both facts are equations of the Kan-extension unit followed by the sheafification unit.

proof.text: For a restricted global sheaf F, the sigma presheaf is the binary product hV × F.obj, by its explicit projections and pair construction. Flat left Kan extension and sheafification preserve binary products. The second projection from each fibre of the preserved product is bijective: joint monicity proves injectivity and the product lift proves surjectivity. These maps form the desired natural isomorphism. Unit naturality for the second projection proves its normalization equation.

theorem unit_normalized_slice_inverse_image
    {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (U : C ⥤ D) [U.IsContinuous J K] [RepresentablyFlat U] (V : C) :
    ∃ (H : Sheaf (J.over V) (Type (u + 1)) ⥤
          Sheaf (K.over (U.obj V)) (Type (u + 1)))
      (η : ∀ F : Sheaf (J.over V) (Type (u + 1)),
        F.obj ⟶ (Over.post U).op ⋙ (H.obj F).obj)
      (e : J.overPullback (Type (u + 1)) V ⋙ H ≅
        Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback U (Type (u + 1)) J K ⋙
          K.overPullback (Type (u + 1)) (U.obj V)),
      (∀ {F G : Sheaf (J.over V) (Type (u + 1))} (f : F ⟶ G),
        f.hom ≫ η G = η F ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (Over.post U).op (H.map f).hom) ∧
      ∀ (F : Sheaf J (Type (u + 1))) (W : C) (q : W ⟶ V) (x : F.obj.obj (op W)),
        (e.hom.app F).hom.app (op (Over.mk (U.map q)))
            ((η (F.over V)).app (op (Over.mk q)) x) =
          ((U.op.lanAdjunction (Type (u + 1))).unit.app F.obj ≫
            Functor.whiskerLeft U.op (toSheafify K (U.op.lan.obj F.obj))).app (op W) x
